articleEn: Why Smart People Often Feel They're Not Smart Enough
articleCn: 為什麼聰明人經常覺得自己不夠聰明

days.topic_en: Quiet Signs of Intelligence — Admitting You Don't Know
days.topic_cn: 聰明的無聲跡象 — 勇於承認「我不知道」

sentences.text: We live in a world that measures intelligence by test scores, quick answers, and loud confidence.

keywords.def: to judge something using a particular standard
bold, noticeable self-assurance

sentences.text: Because of that, it's remarkably easy to go through life assuming you're just average or even falling behind.

keywords.def: to a surprising degree
making less progress than others

sentences.text: In fact, psychology shows that some of the clearest markers of high cognitive ability are subtle habits you might actually see as flaws or quirks.

keywords.def: a sign that shows something exists
not obvious; easy to miss
a small, unusual habit or trait

sentences.text: While insecure people often bluff their way through conversations to sound knowledgeable, you have no problem saying, "I don't know. Tell me more."

keywords.def: to pretend to know in order to get by
knowing a lot about something

sentences.text: It's a hallmark of high intelligence known as intellectual humility.

keywords.def: a typical feature that proves quality or identity
accepting the limits of what you know

sentences.text: Smart minds view gaps in their knowledge not as a threat to their ego, but as an opportunity to learn something new.

keywords.def: something you do not yet know
your sense of your own importance

vocab.def: not obvious; needing careful attention to notice
a small, unusual habit or feature of a person
to pretend to know or be able, in order to get past a situation
a typical sign or feature that shows what something is
the quality of accepting the limits of your own knowledge

speaking.en: Do you think test scores and quick answers are good ways to measure intelligence? Why or why not?
speaking.cn: 你認為考試分數和快速回答是衡量智力的好方法嗎？為什麼？

speaking.en: Have you ever assumed you were just average or falling behind? What made you feel that way?
speaking.cn: 你曾經覺得自己只是普通人，甚至落後別人嗎？是什麼讓你有這種感覺？

speaking.en: When you don't know something in a conversation, do you admit it or bluff your way through?
speaking.cn: 在對話中遇到不懂的事情時，你會承認還是蒙混過去？

speaking.en: Why do you think saying "I don't know" feels risky for many people?
speaking.cn: 為什麼你覺得對很多人來說，說「我不知道」感覺很冒險？

speaking.en: Can you describe a time when a gap in your knowledge became an opportunity to learn something new?
speaking.cn: 你能描述一次「知識缺口」變成學習新事物機會的經驗嗎？

days.topic_en: Self-Talk & Sensory Overload — A Busy, Sensitive Brain
days.topic_cn: 自我對話與感官超載 — 忙碌而敏感的大腦

sentences.text: If you catch yourself talking through your thoughts out loud while solving a problem or organizing your day, don't worry, you're not losing it.

keywords.def: to suddenly notice you are doing something
to go crazy or lose control (informal)

sentences.text: Cognitive research shows that self-talk isn't a sign of craziness.

keywords.def: speaking to yourself, silently or out loud
behavior that seems mentally unstable

sentences.text: Verbalizing your thoughts helps quiet mental clutter, sharpens focus, and accelerates complex problem-solving.

keywords.def: to express thoughts in words
too many disorganized thoughts in your head
to make something clearer or more effective

sentences.text: Do you struggle to focus when there's background chatter, a flickering light, or a cluttered room?

keywords.def: other people's talking around you
messy; filled with too many things

sentences.text: Highly intelligent brains possess superior sensory processing and pattern awareness.

keywords.def: to have or own
how the brain handles sights, sounds and other input

sentences.text: Because your mind naturally processes far more environmental data than average, noisy or chaotic surroundings can cause sensory overload much faster.

keywords.def: completely disordered and confusing
when your senses receive more input than you can handle

vocab.def: to express thoughts or feelings in spoken words
too many disorganized thoughts filling your mind
untidy; covered with too many things
a state where your senses receive more input than you can process
in a state of complete disorder and confusion

speaking.en: Do you ever talk to yourself out loud while solving a problem? Does it actually help you?
speaking.cn: 你解決問題時會大聲自言自語嗎？這真的有幫助嗎？

speaking.en: What helps you quiet the mental clutter when your head feels too full?
speaking.cn: 當腦袋覺得太滿的時候，什麼方法能幫你安靜下那些雜亂的思緒？

speaking.en: How well can you focus in a noisy cafe or a cluttered room?
speaking.cn: 在吵雜的咖啡廳或雜亂的房間裡，你能專注到什麼程度？

speaking.en: What kind of environment do you need to do your best work? Describe it.
speaking.cn: 你需要什麼樣的環境才能做出最好的工作表現？請描述一下。

speaking.en: Have you ever experienced sensory overload? What did you do to recover?
speaking.cn: 你曾經歷過感官超載嗎？你做了什麼來恢復？

days.topic_en: Pivot & Curiosity — Fluid Intelligence at Work
days.topic_cn: 隨機應變與好奇心 — 流動智力的展現

sentences.text: When unexpected problems pop up, some people freeze or panic.

keywords.def: to appear suddenly
to suddenly stop moving or acting

sentences.text: But if your natural instinct is to pivot, adjust your strategy, and find a workaround, that's a direct reflection of fluid intelligence.

keywords.def: to quickly change direction or approach
an alternative way to get past a problem
the ability to solve new problems without prior knowledge

sentences.text: Intelligence isn't just about what you've memorized, it's about how quickly you can navigate brand new, unpredictable situations.

keywords.def: to find your way through something difficult
impossible to know in advance

sentences.text: Where others see mundane everyday things, you see complex systems.

keywords.def: ordinary and not interesting
structures with many connected parts

sentences.text: You find yourself asking why things work the way they do, digging down internet rabbit holes at 1:00 a.m., or wanting to understand the mechanics behind everyday events.

keywords.def: a topic you keep exploring deeper and deeper
the way something works

sentences.text: That relentless intrinsic curiosity is one of the single strongest indicators of high cognitive capacity.

keywords.def: never stopping or weakening
coming from inside yourself, not from outside rewards

vocab.def: to quickly change direction, plan, or strategy
an alternative method to get past a problem or limitation
very ordinary; lacking excitement
to get deeply absorbed in exploring a topic, often online
belonging naturally to something; driven from within

speaking.en: When plans suddenly change, do you freeze, panic, or pivot? Give an example.
speaking.cn: 當計畫突然改變時，你會愣住、恐慌，還是隨機應變？請舉例。

speaking.en: Describe a time you found a workaround for an unexpected problem.
speaking.cn: 描述一次你為突發問題找到替代解法的經驗。

speaking.en: What mundane, everyday thing have you always wondered about how it works?
speaking.cn: 有哪個平凡的日常事物，你一直很好奇它是怎麼運作的？

speaking.en: Have you ever gone down an internet rabbit hole late at night? What was it about?
speaking.cn: 你曾在深夜掉進網路的「兔子洞」嗎？那是關於什麼的？

speaking.en: Which matters more at work: what you have memorized, or how you handle brand new situations? Why?
speaking.cn: 在工作中，哪個比較重要：你記住的知識，還是你應對全新狀況的能力？為什麼？

days.topic_en: Self-Control & Solitude — Delay and Alone Time
days.topic_cn: 自制力與獨處 — 延遲滿足與獨處的力量

sentences.text: Six, you have high self-control and can delay gratification.

keywords.def: the ability to control your actions and desires
to wait for a bigger reward instead of taking a small one now

sentences.text: If you're able to resist short-term temptations in order to achieve a bigger, long-term goal, your brain is functioning at an advanced level.

keywords.def: to refuse something attractive but unhelpful
an aim that takes a long time to achieve

sentences.text: Psychological studies, including the famous marshmallow test, consistently show a strong link between high intelligence and the ability to exercise self-regulation and long-term planning.

keywords.def: controlling your own behavior and emotions
a close connection between two things

sentences.text: Seven, you enjoy spending time completely alone.

keywords.def: with no other people at all

sentences.text: While social connection is essential, people with high cognitive ability often report higher life satisfaction when they spend plenty of time by themselves.

keywords.def: absolutely necessary
how happy you feel about your life overall

sentences.text: Solitude gives your brain the necessary space to process complex ideas, digest information, and recharge without the constant drain of external social stimuli.

keywords.def: the state of being alone, often by choice
to get your energy back
something that gradually uses up your energy

vocab.def: to resist a small reward now in order to gain a bigger reward later
something attractive that you want but should probably avoid
the ability to manage your own behavior and emotions
the state of being alone, especially when peaceful and chosen
to rest in order to get back your energy

speaking.en: Have you ever given up a short-term temptation for a long-term goal? What was it?
speaking.cn: 你曾為了長期目標而放棄眼前的誘惑嗎？那是什麼？

speaking.en: How do you stop yourself from checking your phone when you need to focus?
speaking.cn: 需要專注時，你如何克制自己不去滑手機？

speaking.en: Do you enjoy spending time completely alone? What do you usually do?
speaking.cn: 你喜歡完全獨處的時光嗎？你通常會做什麼？

speaking.en: How do you recharge after a socially draining day?
speaking.cn: 在社交耗盡能量的一天之後，你如何充電？

speaking.en: Do you think self-control can be trained like a muscle? How would you train it?
speaking.cn: 你認為自制力可以像肌肉一樣訓練嗎？你會怎麼訓練它？

days.topic_cn: 懷疑自己 — 鄧寧-克魯格效應

sentences.text: Eight, you assume you're not that smart.

keywords.def: to believe something without proof

sentences.text: Ironically, the ultimate proof of intelligence is doubting it.

keywords.def: in a way opposite to what you would expect
the strongest possible evidence

sentences.text: Known as the Dunning-Kruger effect, people with limited knowledge often overestimate their abilities, while highly intelligent people are so hyper-aware of how vast the world is that they constantly underestimate themselves.

keywords.def: to think something is bigger or better than it is
extremely conscious of something
extremely large

sentences.text: If you routinely worry that you aren't smart enough, that awareness itself proves you are.

keywords.def: as a regular habit
knowledge or understanding of a situation

sentences.text: If you recognized yourself in these points, it's time to stop selling yourself short.

keywords.def: to undervalue your own abilities

sentences.text: Your brain might operate differently than what traditional standards praise, but those subtle habits are proof of a sharp, capable mind.

keywords.def: to work or function
to express approval or admiration

vocab.def: to judge something as greater or better than it really is
to judge something as smaller or worse than it really is
extremely and sometimes excessively conscious of something
to undervalue yourself and your abilities
regularly; as a normal part of life

speaking.en: Do you tend to overestimate or underestimate your own abilities? Why do you think that is?
speaking.cn: 你傾向高估還是低估自己的能力？你覺得原因是什麼？

speaking.en: Have you ever met someone with limited knowledge who was extremely confident? What happened?
speaking.cn: 你遇過知識有限卻非常自信的人嗎？發生了什麼事？

speaking.en: When you worry you're not good enough at something, how do you talk yourself through it?
speaking.cn: 當你擔心自己不夠好時，你會怎麼跟自己對話度過？

speaking.en: In what part of your life have you been selling yourself short?
speaking.cn: 在生活的哪個部分，你一直低估了自己？

speaking.en: After studying this article all week, which of the eight quiet signs do you see most in yourself, and has it changed how you judge your own intelligence?
speaking.cn: 讀完這篇文章一週後，八個無聲跡象中你在自己身上最常看到哪一個？它改變了你評價自己智力的方式嗎？
